notes: TIER: HTTP-first (tier 1) succeeded and was sufficient; tier 2 attempted and genuinely blocked, tier 3 not needed. Direct plain curl/requests to noon.com timed out at TCP/TLS (intermittent IPv4 egress on this workstation per project history); curl_cffi with Chrome impersonation connected cleanly (200s) confirming the site itself is reachable and this was a client-fingerprint issue, not a real block. robots.txt checked first: wildcard group disallows only /_svc/ and /_vs/; the ClaudeBot-specific group has 'Allow: /' with no restriction and no opt-out -- proceeded. Playwright (tier 2) was tried as a cross-check (net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR / full connection timeout on noon.com while the same Playwright instance loaded google.com fine in the same run) -- a genuine tier-2 block, so tier 1 (curl_cffi) remained the working method and tier 3 (Claude-in-Chrome) was not required since tier 1 gave complete, verifiable data via the site's own structured SSR search payload (React-stream 'nbHits'/'facets' JSON embedded in the served HTML, not client-only data -- cross-checked by comparing a known-good category, Christmas Trees, nbHits:561, against the near-100%-fuzzy-matched raw ?q= search endpoint, which is proven unreliable/inflated, e.g. 'hanukkah decor' returned nbHits:1510 and 'valentine decor' returned nbHits:109542 on a UAE site with no such categories -- search-endpoint counts were therefore NOT used as evidence anywhere in this record; only structured category-tree nodes with an id_category were trusted). DISCOVERY METHOD: fetched sitemap-index.xml -> sitemap-ae-categories-0.xml (5,760 category PLP URLs for UAE) and keyword-scanned the full list (christmas, halloween, diwali, ramadan, eid, thanksgiving, valentine, new-year, deepavali, navratri, hanukkah, easter, xmas, noel, national-day, turkey, menorah, pumpkin, wreath, ornament, santa, snowman, advent, tinsel, garland, stocking) both site-wide and restricted to /home-and-kitchen/ (950 URLs) and /home-and-kitchen/home-decor/ (148 URLs) specifically. Also checked the 4 'top-categories_brands' combo sitemaps (~93K category+brand URLs) for the same keywords, and checked the Home Decor department root page's rendered 'trending searches' widget and homepage for any holiday mentions not present in sitemaps. RESULTS -- included: 'Christmas Trees' (home-and-kitchen/home-decor/artificial-flora/christmas-trees/), a real structured category node, nbHits:561, standard 'Best Price Offers' category-page template. 'Outdoor Holiday Decorations' (home-and-kitchen/patio-lawn-and-garden/outdoor-decor/outdoor-holiday-decorations/), also a real structured category node (id_category:49592) with nbHits:8724 and the same category-page template; its brand facet list mixes clearly Christmas-only brands (Kaemingk, 'CHRISTMAS MAGIC') with clearly Halloween-only brands/labels ('Halloween', Gemmy, Joiedomi) -- flagged MANUAL REVIEW because the site names this node generically as 'Holiday' rather than one specific occasion and does not split it further; matches the recurring generic-seasonal-label pattern noted in qa_notes.md item 2, but unlike that pattern this node IS explicitly holiday-named by the site (not merely a seasonal color/style word), so it was included rather than excluded. EXCLUDED and why: 'Seasonal Decor' (home-and-kitchen/home-decor/seasonal-decor-16011/) is a real taxonomy node but returns nbHits:0 with empty facets -- confirmed genuine (not a fetch/render failure) by cross-checking the identical SSR mechanism against Christmas Trees, which correctly returned a real non-zero count in the same run; treated as legit-zero/orphaned and excluded, consistent with project convention. Generic home-decor-accents nodes that plausibly carry holiday-heavy inventory but are NOT holiday-named by the site itself -- 'Home Decor Ornaments', 'Wreath Hangers', 'Tree Skirts', 'Decorative Swags', 'Cardboard Cutouts' (all under home-decor-accents) and 'Garage Door Decorations' (under patio-lawn-and-garden/outdoor-decor) -- title tags and meta descriptions confirmed generic, no holiday reference; excluded per the 'seasonal products in a normal category is not a seasonal category' rule. Diwali/Halloween/Valentine 'trending search' landing pages surfaced on the Home Decor root page (/uae-en/ts-ae-en-diwali-decor/, ts-ae-en-diwali-lantern/, ts-ae-en-diwali-lights/, ts-ae-en-halloween-pumpkin/, plus Valentine's-flower variants) were individually fetched and inspected: their title-tag pattern is 'X UAE | 30-75% OFF' (a deals/search-landing template, distinct from the genuine category template seen on Christmas Trees/Outdoor Holiday Decorations) and their hit counts are in the same inflated, unscoped range as the proven-unreliable raw search endpoint (10K-40K+, clearly not Home-Decor-scoped); classified as marketing/search-landing pages, not genuine site-taxonomy PLPs, and excluded. No Eid, Ramadan, Diwali (as a real category, vs. the excluded trending-search page), Thanksgiving, Easter, Hanukkah, or New Year structured category exists anywhere in the Home & Kitchen department per this exhaustive keyword scan of the category sitemap tree -- absence is not based on search-box zero-results (which would be an invalid test here anyway, and in fact the opposite failure mode: this site's raw search returns false-positive noise, not false-negative absence) but on the actual category-tree enumeration.

rows.evidence: Site SSR search payload embedded in PLP HTML: nbHits:561, nbHitsText:"500+", real structured category node (id_category present) under home-and-kitchen/home-decor/artificial-flora/christmas-trees; page title 'Christmas Trees UAE | Best Price Offers | Dubai, Abu Dhabi'

Site SSR search payload embedded in PLP HTML: nbHits:8724, nbHitsText:"8K+", real structured category node id_category:49592 under home-and-kitchen/patio-lawn-and-garden/outdoor-decor/outdoor-holiday-decorations; page title 'Outdoor Holiday Decorations UAE | Best Price Offers'; brand facet list mixes Christmas-only brands (Kaemingk, 'CHRISTMAS MAGIC') and Halloween-only brands/labels ('Halloween', Gemmy, Joiedomi)
rows.flag: ADJUDICATED KEEP: genuine site-taxonomy node explicitly named 'Holiday' (not a bare seasonal-color/style word) with real qty/evidence; the site itself mixes Christmas and Halloween product lines under this one node with no further split available, so the specific single occasion is irreducibly ambiguous -- kept as a permanent judgment call, category normalized to 'Holiday'.
